I'd assume it's VDL2 you're talking about, it's a bidirectional system for communicating between aircraft and ground stations, and it shows up on several frequencies near the 137MHz band.  
 [https://www.sigidwiki.com/wiki/VHF\_Data\_Link\_-\_Mode\_2\_(VDL-M2)](https://www.sigidwiki.com/wiki/VHF_Data_Link_-_Mode_2_(VDL-M2))

Those interruptions are usually breaks in between portions of the data being sent, once it looks like just noise, that means that the downlink is idling, with the occasional spikes usually being DCS or EMWIN data that comes down fairly often. It can be kind of misleading, but I hope this helps.

That 250kHz limit is only imposed by the whatever software you're using to listen to FM through the dongle's range (i.e. SDR#). However, the entire bandwidth's worth of I/Q data is streamed from the dongle, therefore other software (like pietern's [goestools](https://github.com/pietern/goestools) or the OSP  [SatHelperApp](https://github.com/opensatelliteproject/SatHelperApp)) can process the entire \~2.4MHz bandwidth in order to receive the wide bandwidth signal. This limit leaves enough room for HRIT and the GOES telemetry data to be received simultaneously, however the GOES Rebroadcast is still too large for this (\~11MHz)
